lessons: Development runs exhausted the 1100-action limit with zero or partial scores; use a finite worklist rather than open-ended manipulation loops.
Parse scene names at the final underscore and compare category strings, not numeric instance suffixes.
Assign each observed category a distinct observed basket; do not encode layout-specific destinations.
Scene instance names are not persistent identities. Refresh perception and match a pending target by category and nearby observed position.
Normalize supplied downward quaternions and honor the minimum contact height and basket release height.
Primitive completion does not confirm grasp or task success. Stop on uncertain execution instead of retrying manipulation.

rationale: The policy replaces unbounded behavior with one finite pass over observed objects, assigns separate baskets by category, refreshes target positions, and uses staged pick-and-place motions with normalized orientations. It avoids layout assumptions, hidden state, and speculative manipulation retries. The supplied feedback establishes budget exhaustion but does not identify a specific grasp failure; this revision therefore emphasizes bounded execution and perception-grounded planning without claiming completion.
